title: What If GPS Stopped Working for a Month?

scenes.text: What if GPS stopped for a month? Your map app is the smallest problem.
GPS satellites broadcast time accurate to forty billionths of a second. Finance, phone networks and weather monitoring depend on those clocks.
Telecom service would start to degrade within one to two days, and networks might begin failing after about two weeks.
Ships could still navigate, but port delays would cost the maritime industry over ten billion dollars.
Farm machinery guided by GPS would suffer most in planting season, when the daily cost rises from one billion dollars to one and a half.
A thirty-day outage would cost the U.S. thirty to forty-five billion dollars. One economist calls a billion a day the floor, not the ceiling.
